name: Scythians
place: the steppe from the Danube to the Altai
desc: Horse-archer nomads of the great steppe, who lived in felt tents on wagons, decorated everything with golden animals, steamed themselves with hemp, buried their kings under huge mounds with their horses, and outran the army of Persia.
source: Herodotus, Histories book 4; royal kurgans such as Tovsta Mohyla and Arzhan; the frozen tombs of Pazyryk in the Altai

belligerent: shot backwards from a galloping horse and hit the man chasing me
gluttonous: milked forty mares in one morning for the cheese
devout: laid out willow rods on the ground and read what was to come

inventions.name: Recurve Bow
inventions.source: The short Scythian bow of wood, horn and sinew, carried in a gorytos, a combined bow-case and quiver
inventions.desc: A short bow of wood, horn and sinew that shoots far from horseback: +2 attack, hunting is 10% faster.
inventions.hint: Needs Hide Tailoring, and many hunts.

inventions.name: Hemp Steam Tent
inventions.source: Herodotus 4.75: Scythians threw hemp seed on red-hot stones in a felt tent 'and howl with joy'; braziers with hemp were found in the Pazyryk tombs
inventions.desc: A felt tent over red-hot stones and hemp seed, for washing and for joy: +3 mood, the sick recover 5% faster.

inventions.name: Felt Tents
inventions.source: Herodotus and Hippocrates describe Scythian families living in felt-covered wagons; felt hangings survive at Pazyryk
inventions.desc: Thick felt pressed from wool and stretched over wagons and frames: the cold bites 15% less.
inventions.hint: Needs Hide Tailoring, and many evenings of work.

inventions.name: Golden Animal Style
inventions.source: The gold pectoral of Tovsta Mohyla (4th century BCE) and countless plaques of stags, panthers and griffins
inventions.desc: Stags, panthers and griffins in gold on every quiver, bridle and belt: +2 mood, rites bring 5% more devotion.

foods.name: Mare's Milk Cheese
foods.source: Hippocrates and Herodotus mention hippake, a cheese made from mare's milk, as the Scythians' food
foods.desc: Mare's milk churned and pressed into cheese that rides along in the saddlebags: hunger grows 10% slower, food spoils 5% slower.

foods.name: Cauldron Stew
foods.source: Herodotus 4.61: lacking wood, Scythians boiled meat in a cauldron over a fire of the animal's own bones
foods.desc: Meat boiled in a great bronze cauldron for the whole camp: hunger grows 5% slower, +2 mood.

finds.name: Wild Hemp
finds.desc: Tall plants whose fibre makes cloth and whose seeds make a joyful smoke.

finds.name: Mountain Gold
finds.source: Herodotus wrote of gold-guarding griffins in the far north-east, perhaps the gold of the Altai
finds.desc: Gold in the far mountains, which the old stories say griffins guard.

people.name: Kasta
people.desc: She can pitch a camp of forty tents before the sun is high.
memory: sewed a felt hanging of a griffin and a stag that took a whole winter

people.name: Arpo
people.desc: He was put on a horse before he could walk.
memory: shot a running deer from a galloping horse at a hundred paces

people.name: Targitaos
people.desc: The first man of the Scythians, son of the sky god and a daughter of the river, whose three sons became the fathers of the tribes.

people.name: The Ice Maiden
people.source: A woman buried in the permafrost of the Ukok plateau, Altai, c. 500 BCE, found in 1993
people.desc: A young woman buried with six saddled horses, a tall headdress and her arms covered in tattoos of deer with griffin beaks.

people.name: Anacharsis
people.source: Herodotus 4.76; later Greeks counted him among the wise men of the world
people.text: a Scythian prince who has travelled among the Greeks and come home full of strange ideas, and sharp sayings.
memory: said that laws are like spiderwebs: they catch the weak and the strong break through
people.desc: A Scythian philosopher of the 6th century BCE, remembered by the Greeks for his blunt wisdom.

people.name: Tomyris
people.label: Tomyris, Queen of the Massagetae
people.desc: The queen who defeats the great king of Persia. Combat 9.

people.name: Idanthyrsus
people.label: Idanthyrsus, who Mocked Darius
people.desc: A king who wins by never standing still. Combat 7, Lore 5, very fast.

people.name: Colaxais
people.label: Colaxais, Keeper of the Golden Gifts
people.desc: The youngest son, who could pick up the burning gold. Lore 6, Crafting 6.

events.title: The Great King Comes
events.source: Herodotus 4.83–142: Darius invaded Scythia around 513 BCE; the Scythians retreated, burning the grass and filling the wells, until he gave up
events.text: A huge army from the south has crossed the river. It is far too big to fight. The elders say: we have no towns to defend; let us ride ahead of it, burn the grass, fill the wells, and let the steppe fight for us.

options.label: Ride ahead and burn the grass

do.feat: Outran the army of the Great King

options.result: For months the enemy follows smoke and empty wells. At last they turn back, starving.

options.label: Send tribute
options.result: The great king accepts the gifts and goes home. The young warriors are ashamed.

events.title: The Daughters Ride to War
events.source: Herodotus' 'Amazons' of the Sauromatians; about a third of Scythian-Sarmatian warrior graves with weapons are of women
events.text: The young women have been practising with the bow as long as the young men, and shoot as straight. They ask to ride with the war band. Among us, the old ones say, this has always been so.

events.title: A Mound for a King
events.source: Herodotus 4.71–72 describes royal burials; the kurgans of Arzhan and Tovsta Mohyla held kings, horses and gold
events.text: The chief has died. His body is carried round the tribes for forty days, and now the mound must be raised, with his horses and his gold around him.

options.label: Raise a great mound
options.result: The mound rises taller than any tree. Riders salute it as they pass.

options.label: A rider's grave
options.result: He is buried with his horse and his bow, and the grass covers him.

tales.name: The Golden Gifts from the Sky
tales.text: Four golden things fell from the sky: a plough, a yoke, an axe and a cup. The eldest son went to pick them up, and they burst into flame. The second son went, and they burned again. When the youngest came near, the fire went out, and he carried them home. So his brothers gave him the kingship.
tales.moral: the gifts choose who is worthy

tales.name: A Bird, a Mouse, a Frog and Five Arrows
tales.text: The great king who chased the Scythians across the steppe was sent a strange gift: a bird, a mouse, a frog and five arrows. His advisers read it this way: unless you fly like birds, hide in the earth like mice or leap into the lakes like frogs, our arrows will find you. He went home.
tales.moral: a message can be sharper than an arrow

tales.name: Tomyris and the Great King
tales.text: The conqueror of half the world asked the queen of the steppe to marry him, but she knew he wanted her land, not her. He tricked her son with a feast of wine and captured him. The queen sent a message: give back my son, or I will give you more blood than you can drink. He did not listen, and she kept her word.
tales.moral: do not mistake a queen for a prize

tales.name: The Griffins and the Gold
tales.text: Far to the north-east, past the one-eyed Arimaspians, griffins guard mountains of gold. The one-eyed men are always trying to steal it, and the griffins are always chasing them away. Every golden stag on our belts, the old ones say, was won from a griffin.
